potentialConflicts.description: Both specifications modify Session. activity-state-transformation-tracking adds state capture, metabob-session-tracking adds lifecycle tracking. These are orthogonal concerns.
potentialConflicts.resolution: No conflict - tracking and state capture are independent. Session.createNext() can handle both. Verify both hooks execute correctly.

potentialConflicts.description: Session.close() now records completion metrics. If impulse tracking also hooks session close, order matters.
potentialConflicts.resolution: Impulse tracking happens during session (not at close). No actual conflict detected.

potentialConflicts.description: metabob-session-tracking requires Session.close() call in cleanupActivitySession. activity-state-transformation-tracking also uses this method. Need to ensure close() is called at correct point.
potentialConflicts.resolution: RECOMMENDATION: Call Session.close() BEFORE Activity.unregisterSession() to ensure stats are captured while session is still active.

changes: Adds activity state capture in createNext()

sharedComponents.impactAnalysis: Session is central to all specifications. Current changes are additive (no modifications to existing logic). Session.createNext() can accommodate multiple post-creation hooks. Risk of conflict is LOW.
sharedComponents.recommendation: Establish hook execution order: 1) State capture, 2) Event publishing, 3) Tracking. All are fire-and-forget.

sharedComponents.impactAnalysis: Multiple specs use MCP client for different tools. No conflict as MCP is stateless tool registry.
sharedComponents.recommendation: No action required - MCP client is designed for multi-tool usage
